Good web design in Lubbock, TX starts with a fact every owner in town already knows: a lot of your customers are not from Lubbock. They farm out past the county line, they live in a smaller town with no parts store or specialist, or they are bringing a family member to an appointment. Before they spend an hour on the road, they want to know you are open, that you have what they need, and whether to call first. A website that answers those three things saves them a wasted trip and saves you the phone call.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes every page by hand from Big Sandy. You see a free demo first. The price is printed below and paid once.

Why the Hub City gets so many out-of-town searches

Lubbock is called the Hub City because it serves as the business, school and health care center for the wide stretch of West Texas known as the South Plains. Texas A&M AgriLife Extension describes the city as the major retail and wholesale trade area for West Texas and eastern New Mexico, and as home to the region's major health care providers, including Covenant Health System and the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center.

Farming is part of that draw. A Texas Historical Commission marker calls Lubbock the center of the South Plains cotton industry, one of the leading cotton regions in the country. Gins, equipment dealers, seed and chemical suppliers, irrigation services and the shops that serve farm families all count on customers who measure distance in miles of farm road. Those customers search on their phones the night before, and they notice when a site has the wrong hours.

What someone driving in from Levelland checks before leaving home

These are the answers we put near the top of a Lubbock site, because they decide whether the trip happens at all.

  • Today's hours, including the odd ones. Early opening during harvest, a Saturday close at noon, the week you shut for inventory. If the site and your Google listing disagree, people assume the worst.
  • What you keep on hand. Not a full catalog, just the lines you always stock and the items that run out. A sentence like "call by 10 and we will hold it at the counter" is worth more than a dozen product photos.
  • When to call ahead. Repairs that need a diagnosis slot, special orders, large quantities, a vet or clinic that takes appointments only. Say it plainly so nobody drives in for nothing.
  • The towns you go out to. If your crews travel to Wolfforth, Shallowater, Slaton or Idalou, list them by name, along with anywhere you do not go.
  • How to find the door. Which side street to turn on, where trailers can park, which entrance is for pickups. Small directions matter more to a stranger than to a regular.
  • One tap to call. A phone number that dials from a phone screen, near the top of every page.

Four kinds of Lubbock visitor, four different first questions

The same site has to work for people who arrive for very different reasons. Writing for each of them is most of the job.

Who is comingWhy they are in townWhat they look for on your site
A farm family from a neighboring countyParts, supplies, a repair, a big shopping dayHours, stock, whether a trailer fits in the lot, a direct number for the parts counter
A Texas Tech student or parentMoving in, visiting, finding a regular barber, mechanic or dentistDistance from campus, walk-in or appointment, prices stated up front
A patient's relativeA specialist visit or a hospital staySomewhere to eat, a pharmacy, a place to stay, and how late each one is open
A Lubbock residentA home repair or a service close to homeWhether you cover their side of town, how soon you can come, how to book

Texas Tech alone is a large audience. The university reported a record fall 2025 enrollment of 42,272 students, and a good number of those students and their parents start each year with no local habits at all. A barber, a tire shop or a coffee bar near campus is competing for those first visits every August.

Web design Lubbock TX owners can use in the Depot District, on Broadway or out south

Google says local results come down to relevance, distance and prominence: whether your listing matches the search, how close you are to the searcher or the place they typed, and how well known you are. The distance part is why naming your part of town helps. A restaurant in the Depot District, the entertainment area that is home to the Buddy Holly Center in a former train depot, is found by different searches than a print shop on Broadway downtown or a pediatric dentist in south Lubbock.

Some of those areas are changing fast. The Overton area between downtown and the Texas Tech campus was rebuilt through a privately funded redevelopment and is now a dining, retail and lodging area popular with students. Downtown is drawing investment too: in July 2025 the Lubbock Economic Development Alliance said property value in the Central Business District Tax Reinvestment Zone had grown from $106 million to $297 million. New neighbors bring new competitors, and the one with the clearer site tends to get the first call.

A home service company has the opposite problem from a downtown shop: you go to the customer. For an HVAC, roofing or plumbing outfit, the service area page does the heavy lifting. Name the neighborhoods and towns you work in, how far out you will drive for a no-cooling call in July, and whether there is a trip charge past a certain point. Those plain answers are what people in Wolfforth or Slaton look for before they call someone forty minutes away.

A walk-through: a portrait studio whose clients come from three counties

Picture a typical Lubbock photographer working out of a small studio. Many sessions are families who drive in from smaller towns for senior portraits or holiday photos, and they book weeks ahead. Here is how we would plan that site, page by page.

  1. HomeThe kinds of sessions offered, starting prices if the owner wants them shown, and a booking button above the fold.
  2. SessionsOne section per session type: how long it runs, what to wear, how many edited images come back, and how long that takes.
  3. Getting hereStudio address, parking, and a note for families coming in from out of town about how early to arrive.
  4. Service areaThe towns clients come from and whether the photographer travels to them for on-location work.
  5. ContactA short form that emails the request straight to the owner, plus the phone number.

That is a five-page Starter site. Nothing on it is filler, and every page answers a question the owner hears on the phone each week.

Free help for South Plains owners

Northwest Texas SBDC

Hosted at Texas Tech, the Northwest Texas Small Business Development Center network serves 95 counties through six regional centers, with no-cost advising for people starting or growing a business.

Lubbock Chamber of Commerce

The chamber represents member businesses across the South Plains and runs networking events, committees on agriculture and transportation, and a Leadership Lubbock program.

Lubbock Economic Development Alliance

LEDA was created by the Lubbock City Council and is funded by the economic development share of local sales tax. Its work centers on recruiting, keeping and expanding employers in the city.

Common questions

How much does web design in Lubbock, TX cost?

Quotes vary a lot depending on who builds the site and how they bill. Ours are printed: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep an AI agent, and $49 a month without one. You see a free demo of your site before you pay anything.

Can my website name the towns around Lubbock that I serve?

Yes, and for a South Plains business it usually should. Starter includes a service area page that lists the towns you cover, such as Wolfforth, Shallowater, Levelland or Slaton. Pro adds ten city pages, each one researched and written for a single town, so the Levelland page says something true about Levelland instead of swapping one name for another.

Should a Lubbock store put its inventory on the website?

Not necessarily the whole inventory. Our packages do not include an online store or a shopping cart, and many shops do not need one. What helps a customer driving in from another county is a plain list of what you usually carry, what sells out, and when to call ahead to have something set aside. That list is easy to keep current.

Who does web design in Lubbock without a long contract?

We do. The site price is one payment and you own the finished site. The only ongoing charges are optional: hosting, maintenance and updates at $49 a month, waived while you keep an AI agent, and the AI chat widget or phone agent at $297 a month if you choose to keep one after the free trial. You can cancel the agent any time.

Not us. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson in Big Sandy, East Texas, and every site is built remotely. You reach him by phone, email and shared links. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.
